text:
maria: Quick heads-up  I'm starting a small canonical page that merges our various autoscale examples (steady, burst, reserved pools). Plan to remove duplicated YAMLs across the dedicated docs. PR later today, tagging reviewers. @devon @samir any concerns?

devon: Sounds good. Suggest separate subsections for burst vs steady policies + a visual table comparing trade-offs.

samir: No objections. Please include tenant-label examples and explain eviction priority interaction  that's where folks get tripped up.

maria: Will do. Outline: steady, burst, reserved-pool, tenant-labeling+eviction notes, short Terraform and SDK snippets. Send any code you want copied verbatim.

jen: I can craft Node + Python SDK snippets. Prefer tiny runnable examples (createScalePolicy call).

samir: Minimal burst YAML that you can paste in:

```yaml
scalePolicy:
  name: burst-warmup
  type: reactive
  targets:
    cpu_utilization: 0.75
  burst:
    max_instances: 10
    cooldown: 60s
  labels:
    tenant: "analytics"
```

maria: Nice. Also want to show a mapping table: label isolation=dedicated -> eviction_priority=high, isolation=shared -> eviction_priority=low.

teo: One thing: we need consistent SLA phrasing in the docsdistinguish "SLA-backed reserved pools" from "best-effort autoscale". Docs asked for one-liner we can copy into multiple pages.

maria: Good call. I'll add a standard SLA blurb and link to the draft: https://redwood-internal/handbook/dedicated-sla#draft

docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4357 - autoscale-canonical-page + snippets. CI: docs-lint passing, linkcheck: 1 warn (old TF anchor).

devon: Which anchor? I can add a redirect or adjust the anchor in the target page.

docs-bot: Broken anchor: /docs/dedicated/provisioning#terraform-examples -> 404 anchor (page exists).

devon: I'll patch in a tiny redirect on the provisioning page. Pushing in a minute.

jen: SDK Node snippet (paste for the page):

```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.dedicated.createScalePolicy({
  poolId: 'pool-123',
  name: 'burst-warmup',
  policy: { type: 'reactive', targets: { cpu: 0.75 }, burst: { max_instances: 10, cooldown: '60s' } },
});
```

maria: Thanks. I'll include Node + Python + HCL mapping (TF resource -> SDK call). Samir offered to sanity-check the TF formatting.

samir: I'll validate the TF and mention prefer cooldown = "60s". Also add a note on how prefix/KV caching changes effective CPU for batching policies.

maria: Great. Tagging reviewers: @devon @samir @jen. Waiting for the redirect fix before merging. ETA EOD.

devon: :thumbsup:
